models.description:
Overview
Karyukti AI is an Enterprise Multi-Agent Business Automation Platform designed to automate business workflows through collaborative AI agents. Rather than relying on a single AI assistant, the platform orchestrates multiple specialized agents—including Planner, CRM, HR, Workflow, Analytics, Memory, Security, and Report Agents—to solve complex enterprise tasks.
The platform provides a Business Startup Wizard for configuring business context, role-based dashboards (Admin, Manager, Worker), customizable AI agents, workflow automation, CRM management, knowledge integration, and enterprise security features. Its modular architecture allows organizations to configure intelligent business assistants for different industries while maintaining a unified user experience.
Usage
Supported Use Cases
Karyukti AI can be used for:
Business process automation
CRM management
Employee onboarding
Workflow automation
Report generation
Knowledge retrieval
Customer support
Business analytics
Document assistance
Task management
Typical Workflow
Business Selection
        ↓
Role Selection
        ↓
Dashboard
        ↓
Prebuilt Agent
        OR
Custom Agent
        ↓
Multi-Agent Collaboration
        ↓
CRM / Knowledge Base
        ↓
Business Response
Inputs
Business type
User role
User prompt
Uploaded knowledge documents (optional)
CRM context (optional)
Workflow configuration
Outputs
Context-aware business responses
Reports
CRM insights
Workflow actions
Business recommendations
Task summaries
Known Limitations
Response quality depends on available business context and knowledge.
External integrations require proper backend configuration.
Complex business decisions should be reviewed by human users.
The platform is designed to assist users rather than replace human decision-making.
System
Karyukti AI is part of a complete enterprise platform rather than a standalone language model.
Input Requirements
Business configuration
User authentication
User prompt
Optional CRM records
Optional uploaded documents
Downstream Components
CRM Module
Knowledge Base
Workflow Engine
Analytics Dashboard
Role-Based Dashboard
Multi-Agent Coordinator
The Multi-Agent Coordinator distributes tasks among specialized agents and combines their outputs before presenting a final response.
Implementation Requirements
Software
React
TypeScript
Tailwind CSS
Node.js
Express
PostgreSQL
Prisma ORM
Docker
Hardware
The platform can run on a standard development machine:
Dual-core CPU or higher
8 GB RAM (recommended)
PostgreSQL database
Docker (optional)
Inference requirements depend on the configured AI backend. The platform architecture is model-agnostic and supports local or external AI models.
Model Characteristics
Model Initialization
Karyukti AI is not a custom-trained language model. It is a modular enterprise application that coordinates specialized AI agents through configurable workflows and reasoning logic.
Model Statistics
Architecture:
Multi-Agent System
Role-Based Access Control
Workflow Engine
CRM Integration
Knowledge Retrieval
Memory Management
Security Layer
Latency depends on workflow complexity and configured AI backend.
Other Details
The platform supports configurable reasoning workflows and modular agent orchestration. It does not require retraining when new business agents are created.
Data Overview
Business Context
The platform processes organizational information such as:
CRM records
Customer information
Employee records
Business workflows
Uploaded documents
Knowledge Base entries
User prompts
These data sources provide context for business-specific assistance.
Demographic Groups
Karyukti AI is designed as a domain-independent enterprise platform and is intended for organizations across industries. It does not target or optimize for any specific demographic group.
Evaluation Data
No proprietary model training or benchmark datasets were used because the platform focuses on agent orchestration rather than training a new foundation model.
Evaluation Results
Summary
The project has been evaluated through functional testing of enterprise workflows, including:
Multi-agent task coordination
Business Startup Wizard
Role-based access control
CRM operations
Workflow execution
Knowledge retrieval
Theme persistence
Dashboard functionality
The focus of evaluation is on platform functionality, reliability, and user experience.
Subgroup Evaluation
Testing covered multiple business domains including:
Healthcare
Finance
Retail
Education
Manufacturing
Hospitality
Logistics
The platform dynamically adapts its behavior based on the selected business type.
Fairness
Karyukti AI is designed to provide consistent behavior across supported business domains. Access to features is governed by predefined user roles (Admin, Manager, Worker) rather than personal characteristics.
Usage Limitations
The platform is intended to assist enterprise users and should not be used as the sole authority for:
Legal decisions
Medical diagnosis
Financial advice
Regulatory compliance
Human review is recommended for high-impact decisions.
Ethics
The platform incorporates enterprise security and responsible AI practices, including:
JWT Authentication
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Secure session management
Audit logging
Input validation
Prompt filtering
Sensitive data protection
Request validation
Karyukti AI is designed to support human decision-making while promoting transparency, security, and responsible use of AI in enterprise environments.

models.author: SamChyst
models.description:
**Model Summary**

This model is a CatBoost-based regressor engineered to capture market regime indicators and predict one-year realized asset alpha for US equities. It is designed as the market-side view within a broader ["Conditional Alpha Prediction"](https://github.com/SamsonChyst/Conditional-Alpha-Prediction) framework, separating macroeconomic/trading factors from structural fundamental valuations. Instead of outputting a definitive, single trading signal, its point forecasts (alpha_hat) are generated out-of-fold to feed a subsequent copula-based probabilistic fusion layer.

**Usage**

The model is utilized during both the research pipeline (to generate unbiased signals) and the runtime phase (to evaluate live tickers). It operates on tabular data and expects a 2D array or pandas DataFrame as input. Input Shape: (N, 10) where N is the number of assets/observations, and 10 is the fixed number of market features. Output Shape: (N, 1) containing continuous floating-point values representing predicted realized alpha (excess return over the S&P 500 benchmark).

**Known and Preventable Failures:**

Target Shifting: Extreme market anomalies can destabilize training folds. This is mitigated by enforcing a StratifiedKFold split across target quantiles, ensuring stable target distributions during cross-validation.
Overfitting on Noise: Financial time-series data has a low signal-to-noise ratio. To prevent the model from learning noise, early stopping is strictly bound to an independent validation subset (15% of the training split) during the hyperparameter tuning phase.
Look-Ahead Bias: Prevented at the dataset level by anchoring corporate reporting milestones to actual SEC publication dates rather than fiscal year-ends.

**Code Snippet (Loading and Inference)**

import pandas as pd
from catboost import CatBoostRegressor

**Load the trained model artifact**

model = CatBoostRegressor()
model.load_model("Models/market_model.cbm")
Define live features matching the training schema
live_features = pd.DataFrame([{
"beta_ewm_median": 1.15,
"volatility_21d_mean": 0.018,
"volatility_21d_max": 0.032,
"log_volume_mean": 18.2,
"market_deviation_mean": -0.05,
"market_deviation_std": 0.02,
"market_momentum_mean": 0.001,
"market_momentum_std": 0.012,
"market_3y_return": 0.45,
"t_bond_rate": 0.042
}])

**Execute inference**

predicted_alpha_hat = model.predict(live_features)

**System**
The model is not standalone; it is a core component of the Conditional-Alpha-Prediction system.
Input Requirements: Clean, normalized, point-in-time aligned daily market indicators aggregated into yearly metrics, combined with macro regime vectors (10Y Treasury Rate).
Downstream Dependencies: The direct output (alpha_hat) acts as an input variable for the downstream copula engine (copula_logic.py). The copula layer fuses this market prediction with a fundamental DCF-implied upside signal using a Clayton vine copula to model the complete conditional probability distribution of alpha.
Implementation requirements

**Software Environment**
Python 3, CatBoost, Scikit-Learn, Optuna, Pandas, Numpy.
Compute Hardware: Standard consumer CPU (e.g., Intel Core / AMD Ryzen) or basic cloud compute instance.

**Compute Metrics:** Training is highly lightweight due to the shallow tree depth configuration (depth=3) and small tabular feature space. Total optimization time across 50 Optuna trials takes under 2 minutes on a single CPU core. Inference latency is sub-millisecond per ticker, making it highly efficient for interactive runtime report generation. Energy consumption and compute footprints are negligible.

**Model initialization**
The model was trained entirely from scratch using the local historical dataset compilation. No pre-trained weights or transfer learning protocols are applicable to this tabular financial configuration.

**Model stats**
Size on Disk: Less than 1 MB (serialized as an optimized binary .cbm file).
Architecture: Symmetric decision trees (CatBoost default structure).
Hyperparameters: Optimized dynamically using Optuna. Default baseline uses 300 iterations, a shallow tree depth of 3 to bound complexity, a learning rate of 0.05, and an L2 leaf regularization coefficient of 3.0. Loss function is tracked via Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE).

**Data Overview**

**Training data**

The primary data source is train_dataset.csv, a custom tabular matrix compiled by parsing US equity markets. It covers 2,792 parsed tickers, yielding 4,226 total rows of structural data.
Collection: Automated via parser.py using public endpoints from SEC EDGAR Company Facts (annual corporate metrics) and the Yahoo Finance API (historical pricing, volume, and index returns).
Pre-processing: Continuous features were cleaned of infinite values, and missing blocks were systematically dropped. Price metrics were engineered into trailing volatilities, rolling beta medians, and structural momentum deviations.

**Evaluation data**

The validation design uses a strict 5-fold RepeatedKFold strategy repeated across 10 iterations, generating a total of 50 model training cycles to build out-of-fold (OOF) predictions. There is no structural difference between training and evaluation splits, as stratification across alpha-based quantiles ensures that each split mirrors the statistical distribution of the full historical data matrix.

**Evaluation Results**

The market-side model demonstrates that while predicting the absolute magnitude of financial alpha under weak signal-to-noise conditions is inherently difficult, it captures a highly robust and statistically significant monotonic relationship with actual returns.
Latest Stable OOF Performance:
RMSE: 0.3970
Spearman Rank Correlation: 0.3937
Kendall's Tau: 0.2762

# Model Summary

Cerebras-GPT-2.7B is an autoregressive language model developed by Cerebras Systems as part of the Cerebras-GPT family of open language models. With approximately 2.7 billion parameters, it is designed for efficient text generation, language modeling, and natural language processing research while providing an excellent balance between performance and computational efficiency.

The model follows a GPT-3 style decoder-only Transformer architecture and was trained on The Pile dataset using Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling laws (approximately 20 training tokens per parameter). It features a 2048-token context window, uses a Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer, and was trained on the Andromeda AI Supercomputer powered by Cerebras wafer-scale hardware. The Cerebras-GPT family was released to provide fully open and reproducible language models for research, benchmarking, and experimentation.

Cerebras-GPT-2.7B is fully compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers, making it suitable for deployment on local systems, cloud platforms, and Kaggle notebooks.

License: Apache License 2.0.

**Key Features**
2.7B parameter GPT language model
GPT-3 style decoder-only Transformer
Trained using Chinchilla scaling laws
2048-token context window
Trained on The Pile dataset
Optimized for efficient language modeling
Compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers
Fine-tunable for downstream NLP tasks

## Usage

Cerebras-GPT-2.7B is designed for language modeling, text generation, research, prompt engineering, benchmarking, fine-tuning, educational projects, and downstream NLP applications. The model is fully compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers and can be deployed efficiently on local systems or Kaggle notebooks.

## Disclaimer

**Disclaimer:** **Cerebras Systems** and original owners/authors of the model completely reserve the right to contact us regarding the removal of the hosted model.

instances.overview: Cerebras-GPT-2.7B is one of the larger models in the Cerebras-GPT family, offering significantly improved language understanding, reasoning, and text generation compared to the smaller 1.3B, 590M, and 256M variants while remaining practical for research and fine-tuning on modern GPUs. It is well suited for benchmarking, prompt engineering, educational projects, downstream NLP tasks, and large-scale language model experimentation.
instances.usage:
Cerebras-GPT-2.7B is designed for language modeling, text generation, research, prompt engineering, benchmarking, fine-tuning, educational projects, and downstream NLP applications. The model is fully compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers and can be deployed efficiently on local systems or Kaggle notebooks.

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
import torch

model_path = "/kaggle/input/cerebras-gpt-2-7b"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path)

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_path,
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,
    device_map="auto"
)

prompt = "Artificial intelligence is"

inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)

outputs = model.generate(
    **inputs,
    max_new_tokens=150,
    temperature=0.7,
    top_p=0.9,
    do_sample=True
)

print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))

CrisisMind AI is an AI-powered climate intelligence platform that predicts infrastructure risks caused by climate events such as floods, heatwaves, and extreme weather conditions.

## Features
- Real-time climate risk assessment
- Explainable AI recommendations
- Conversational AI Copilot
- Scenario simulation
- Automated report generation
- Global climate monitoring dashboard

## Technologies
- Python
- FastAPI
- Next.js
- Gemini 2.5 Flash
- OpenWeather API
- Open-Meteo API

## Risk Methodology

Overall Risk =
0.40 × Flood Score +
0.35 × Heatwave Score +
0.25 × Infrastructure Score

## Use Cases
- Smart Cities
- Disaster Management
- Infrastructure Planning
- Climate Resilience

models.description:
# Model Summary

OpenELM-3B-Instruct is the largest instruction-tuned model in Apple's OpenELM family. It offers the strongest reasoning, language understanding, and text generation capabilities among the OpenELM models while remaining efficient enough for deployment on modern consumer GPUs. The OpenELM project emphasizes transparency by releasing model weights, training recipes, evaluation tools, and open-source infrastructure to support reproducible AI research and development.

## Usage

OpenELM-3B-Instruct is designed for conversational AI, text generation, reasoning, coding assistance, summarization, question answering, educational applications, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The model is fully compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers, making it suitable for deployment on local machines, Apple Silicon devices, and cloud GPU platforms such as Kaggle.

## Disclaimer

**Disclaimer:** **Apple** and original owners/authors of the model completely reserve the right to contact us regarding the removal of the hosted model.

instances.overview:
OpenELM-3B-Instruct is an instruction-tuned large language model developed by Apple as part of the OpenELM family of efficient open language models. With approximately 3 billion parameters, it is designed to deliver strong instruction-following capabilities while maintaining efficient inference for conversational AI, reasoning, code generation, summarization, question answering, and natural language understanding.

The model is built on a decoder-only Transformer architecture featuring a layer-wise scaling strategy that efficiently allocates parameters across transformer layers to maximize performance without significantly increasing computational cost. OpenELM models were pretrained using Apple's CoreNet framework on approximately 1.8 trillion publicly available tokens, making them suitable for research, education, edge AI, and cloud deployment.

OpenELM-3B-Instruct supports a 2048-token context window and is fully compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers, enabling deployment on local systems, Apple Silicon devices, and cloud platforms such as Kaggle.

License: Apple Machine Learning Research Model License (Apple AMLR License). Please review the official license before using the model for research or commercial applications.

**Key Features**
3B parameter instruction-tuned language model
Trained on approximately 1.8 trillion public tokens
Decoder-only Transformer with layer-wise scaling
2048-token context window
Strong reasoning and instruction-following capabilities
Optimized for conversational AI, coding, and text generation
Compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers
Suitable for Kaggle, Apple Silicon, and local deployment
Fine-tunable for downstream NLP tasks
instances.usage:
OpenELM-3B-Instruct is designed for conversational AI, text generation, reasoning, coding assistance, summarization, question answering, educational applications, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The model is fully compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers, making it suitable for deployment on local machines, Apple Silicon devices, and cloud GPU platforms such as Kaggle.

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
import torch

model_path = "/kaggle/input/openelm-3b-instruct"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    model_path,
    trust_remote_code=True
)

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_path,
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,
    device_map="auto",
    trust_remote_code=True
)

prompt = "Explain artificial intelligence in simple terms."

inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)

outputs = model.generate(
    **inputs,
    max_new_tokens=200,
    temperature=0.7,
    top_p=0.9,
    do_sample=True
)

print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
